small_guidance:
- Reduce shared memory pressure: drop BLOCK_N from 256 to 128 (or BLOCK_M to 64) and lower num_stages from 3 to 2. With BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32, num_stages=2, num_warps=4 the kernel should fit in 100KB shmem on the 4090.
- Add a `triton.autotune` decorator over a small set of configs (128/128/32, 64/128/32, 128/64/64) keyed on (M, N, K) so the tuner can search legal shapes without re-launching with oversized tiles.
- Keep the LSE-partial epilogue fused inside the GEMM kernel (already done) — but make sure `row_max`/`row_sumexp` use `tl.max`/`tl.sum` over axis=1 with the smaller BLOCK_N to avoid an extra shmem spill.
large_guidance:
- The structure (split-K-over-N GEMM producing per-tile (max, sumexp) partials, then a finalize kernel that combines partials and applies the elementwise tail) is sound and faithful to the reference. A from-scratch rewrite is not needed; the failure is purely a shared-memory budget overrun from BLOCK_N=256 × BLOCK_K=64 × num_stages=3 (≈192KB > 101KB limit).
- If a redesign is chosen, consider a single-pass persistent kernel: one program per row group of M, looping the full N internally with online-softmax-style (running max, running sumexp) accumulation, avoiding the partials buffer and the second kernel launch entirely. This trades a wider K-loop for eliminating an intermediate tensor of size M×ntiles_n.
- Alternatively, keep the two-kernel design but make the partial layout `[ntiles_n, M]` (column-major in partials) so the finalize kernel can coalesce loads across the reduction axis with one program per row.
